_comment: Fragment 91 — D-135: a runbook applied in full, a pre-existing conflation fixed at its source while executing, and a fixture whose expectation string diverged from the check's real output. Merged 2026-08-25.

nodes.label: A Pre-Existing Documented Conflation Fixed While Executing an Unrelated Runbook
nodes.description: A prior decision had already named a work-queue removal being described with the same word as a governed archival move, and that specific text was never corrected at its source until a later runbook, executing something else entirely, happened to touch the same file and fixed it in passing.
nodes.rationale: A decision that names a defect does not repair the document it was found in; someone still has to open that file and change the words. Recording that the fix happened as a side effect of unrelated work, rather than claiming it as new analysis, keeps the credit and the timeline honest.

nodes.label: A Fixture's Expected Substring Diverged From the Check's Actual Wording
nodes.description: A fixture asserting that a check produces a specific finding used a paraphrase of that finding's wording rather than an exact substring, so the fixture failed even though the check itself was already firing correctly on the mutation.
nodes.rationale: A fixture proves nothing about the check when its own assertion is wrong; the miss here was in the test, not the mechanism under test, and confirming that distinction before editing anything is what kept a working check from being weakened to satisfy a mistaken expectation.
